headline: Tonight's coastal storm keeps trending lighter and farther east (only a tenth or two of rain for New York City, up to about an inch on eastern Long Island and southeastern Connecticut), while a bigger storm looks likely Wednesday night through Friday, with heavy rain on Thanksgiving, gusts of 35–45 mph and widespread coastal flooding.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Sunday is unusually mild, with forecast highs of 61 at Bridgeport and 63 at Islip, close to the records of 64 for the date. Rain from low pressure passing east-southeast of Long Island comes mainly late this afternoon and evening, but totals keep trending down: only a tenth or two of an inch for New York City and points north and west, possibly none in the far western areas, and up to about an inch on the forks of eastern Long Island and in southeastern Connecticut, where rain is moderate to heavy at times this evening and overnight and where the only marginal risk of flooding rain remains. Winds turn east and then northeast at 10–15 mph with coastal gusts of 25–30 mph, plus a very low chance of brief 40–45 mph gusts right along the coast of eastern Long Island and possibly southeastern Connecticut if the storm tracks close enough. Low clouds thicken this evening, and any lingering showers end by daybreak Monday.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: The storm moves quickly off to the northeast, and Monday turns dry with clearing skies; a cold front passes late Monday afternoon, bringing northwest winds gusting around 15–25 mph. Tuesday stays dry but breezy, with northwest gusts of about 25–30 mph, as a large, strong area of high pressure builds over the Northeast Tuesday into Wednesday. Wednesday looks dry, then clouds lower Wednesday night with a slight chance of rain late and east-northeast winds picking up, gusting 25–35 mph, highest around New York City and along the coast.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Computer models continue to agree on a potentially large, impactful coastal storm Wednesday night through Thanksgiving and Friday, likely worse for wind and coastal flooding than tonight's system because the tight squeeze between it and the strong high pressure to the north will drive strong winds. Gusts of 35–45 mph are possible sometime Thanksgiving Day or Thanksgiving night, and a period of moderate to heavy rain is likely on Thanksgiving, though the storm's fast movement should limit flooding from rain. Friday brings a lingering chance of rain mainly in the morning, with winds turning west and gusting around 30–35 mph. The pattern is complex enough that small changes could shift the storm's strength, track and timing a lot, so forecasters are still monitoring it.

coast: With Monday morning's high tide, there is at worst a minimal coastal flood threat for the south shore back bays of Nassau County, where minor flood levels may just be touched at the most vulnerable spots; a statement may eventually be needed, though the storm's farther-east track and quick movement could keep water levels short. Tides run high with Tuesday's full moon, so many locations need less than a foot of extra water to reach minor flooding, and the current forecast supports widespread minor to moderate coastal flooding, perhaps even localized major flooding, with the Wednesday night–Friday storm, along with beach flooding, erosion and overwash. On the water, a Small Craft Advisory is in effect until 6 PM Monday for the near-shore ocean waters and from 6 PM Sunday to 6 AM Monday for Long Island Sound, the bays and New York Harbor, and a Gale Warning covers the outer ocean waters from 6 PM Sunday to 6 AM Monday, with rough ocean seas lingering into Monday night. After only a brief lull Tuesday afternoon and night, ocean gusts of 29–35 mph (25–30 knots) return by Wednesday afternoon, reaching gale force Wednesday night and storm force on Thursday, with gales reaching the Sound and bays late Wednesday night into Thursday. Waves could build to at least 12–20 feet on the ocean (occasionally 20–25 feet out east), 7–10 feet on western Block Island Sound east of Orient Point, and 4–6 feet on Long Island Sound and at the entrance to New York Harbor.
watch_for: Thanksgiving coastal storm: widespread minor to moderate coastal flooding, possibly locally major, plus beach erosion and overwash, with gusts of 35–45 mph and heavy rain.
Small changes in the Thanksgiving storm's track, strength and timing could make a big difference.
Possible minor flooding on the south shore back bays of Nassau County with Monday morning's high tide.
confidence: Forecasters are increasingly confident tonight's storm stays east, keeping rain light around New York City, and models agree on a significant Thanksgiving storm, but its exact track, strength and timing remain uncertain because of a complex pattern.
